kind: bug / Graph / unsupported builtin / silent wrong result
title: Graph mode silently returns iterator internal state for explicit next(iter(Tensor)) and next(enumerate(Tensor))
duplicate_search_result: No exact matching GitHub or Gitee issue found.
documentation_notes: MindSpore 2.9 static graph syntax documentation lists enumerate among supported built-in functions.
The same MindSpore static graph syntax documentation lists next among unsupported built-in functions.

Because next is documented as unsupported, the expected Graph behavior is to reject the unsupported syntax. Returning an internal (current, rest) iterator protocol object as the user-visible result is still a silent wrong-result bug.
classification_notes: Not a numerical precision issue: the mismatch is a return structure/type mismatch.
Not an unsupported CPU kernel issue: the failing cases compile and return a result; for/list controls over the same Tensor input also succeed.
Not duplicate coverage for Tensor iteration generally: list(enumerate(x))[0][1], for row in x, and for _, row in enumerate(x) all match PyNative mode.
Grouped as one issue because the triggering paths share the same Graph next/iterator protocol leak.
